title: Line origination: model specification
description: A specification, not a validated model. Every free parameter is left blank with the estimator that would fill it; a coefficient appearing here as a number would be a fabrication, so none do. The architecture is deliberately totals-first, availability-adjusted and market-neutral at the base, so the market enters only as a benchmark at the end (that is what makes 'did we beat the close' answerable).

sections.title: A. Pipeline stages
sections.description: Each stage is independently testable and independently releasable; a stage's output is a distribution, never a point, because a point hides the uncertainty that the gates measure.

rows.name: Game spine and calendar
rows.spec: One row per scheduled game: kickoff UTC, venue, dome flag, rest days for each club, short-week flag, bye flag, travel timezones. Rest asymmetry is a fact of the schedule, so it is coded here rather than inferred later.
rows.inputs: Official league schedule and the operations calendar of deadlines (SRC-004, SRC-006); schedule changes are published as league news (a Week 11 schedule change was live on the operations page when we captured it).
rows.output: games.parquet — one row per game with calendar features.

rows.name: Base scoring rate (possessions x efficiency)
rows.spec: E[points] = possessions x points per possession, built separately for each club and each side of the ball, so a total is the sum of two scoring expectations and a spread is their difference. This keeps one model behind both markets instead of two models that can contradict each other.
rows.inputs: Own drive/game logs (GAP-05, not yet available); official box-score level counts once collection is approved.
rows.output: club_scoring: mean and sd of points per game, per side.
rows.params: prior mean, shrinkage weight toward league average, window length (weeks), home/scoring intercept — ALL UNVERIFIED / blank

rows.name: Regression-to-mean shrinkage of priors
rows.spec: Enter the season with a prior shrunk hard toward league average, and let it loosen only with within-season evidence. The published mechanism this defends is over-reaction to previous-season performance in win-total markets; the same failure mode is the natural candidate in week 1-4 spreads.
rows.inputs: Prior seasons' scoring (own logs); no market input.
rows.output: shrunk club priors with a stated variance.
rows.params: shrinkage constant k — UNVERIFIED / blank (fit by maximising out-of-sample log-loss, not by tuning PnL)

rows.name: Availability layer (injuries)
rows.spec: For each club and unit group, compute an availability vector from the official report: Out, Doubtful, Questionable, plus practice trajectory DNP/LP/FP across the week. Players certain to play are absent from the game-status list, so absence is information and must be modelled as such, not treated as a missing value.
rows.inputs: Official injury report per game (SRC-001); definitions and the fact that designations are qualitative (SRC-002); club-side change marking (SRC-021).
rows.output: availability[club, player, group, day] with a capture timestamp per row.
rows.params: P(play | designation, trajectory, position) — estimated, never hard-coded; currently blank

rows.name: Next-Man-Up deficiency (defence and offence)
rows.spec: Deficiency of a unit = sum over absent players of (their expected snap share x the quality gap to the actual replacement). The replacement is chosen from the eligible set the roster rules define (53-man list, 54/55 elevations, IR and PUP/NFI return windows), which is why a fourth-string case can be mechanically derived from transactions even when depth charts are unavailable.
rows.inputs: Roster architecture (SRC-003, SRC-005); availability (S4); own snap-share history for the quality gap.
rows.output: deficiency[club, unit, side] on a common scale (points per game equivalent).
rows.params: group weights (OL, DL, LB, CB/S, WR/TE, RB, QB), quality-gap estimator — ALL UNVERIFIED / blank

rows.name: Quarterback branch
rows.spec: QB1 / QB2 / QB3 handled as a discrete regime, not as another deficiency term, because the quarterback case dominates the others and is the only one that changes a team's whole distribution rather than a slice of it. QB availability may be an input; a wager on whether the QB starts is a prohibited market and is excluded at the compliance gate.
rows.output: qb_regime multiplier on both scoring expectations.
rows.params: regime effect size — UNVERIFIED / blank (must be fitted on our own logs)

rows.name: Context adjustments
rows.spec: Only adjustments with a verified source are allowed: rest and short week (from the schedule), venue and altitude (a static venue attribute), travel days. Weather and officiating are excluded until their sources are verified; that is a feature of the process, not an oversight.
rows.inputs: Schedule (S1); venue list. Weather blocked on GAP-07; officiating blocked by policy (SRC-008).
rows.params: each adjustment's effect size — UNVERIFIED / blank

rows.name: Release and re-price
rows.spec: Five committed releases per game: Tuesday 12:00 ET (after prior week settles), Wednesday evening (first report), Thursday evening, Friday 17:00 ET (after final practice and designations), and Sunday only if an official inactive list is verified from an official source. Each release is stored with the input snapshot hash, so a later review can distinguish 'model changed' from 'news changed'.
rows.inputs: The official report cadence (SRC-001) and the filing deadlines we have verified only as page-observed, not as quoted policy (GAP-09).
rows.params: cut-off before kickoff for staking; recommended -30 min, to be reviewed

rows.name: Market comparison and edge
rows.spec: edge = our expected value minus the market's, expressed both in points and in per-dollar EV after the assumed hold. We benchmark against the operator's closing price, and separately against our own Friday number, to separate 'we are right' from 'we are fast'.
rows.inputs: GAP-01 line history (blocked); measured hold per family (GAP-08, blocked).
rows.output: edge[game, market, release] and a bet/no-bet decision.
rows.params: edge threshold (recommended starting point: bet only when modelled EV clears the break-even hurdle by a stated margin — value to be set by the owner's volume trade-off, not by us)

rows.name: Staking
rows.spec: Fractional Kelly on our own probability, with a per-bet and per-cluster cap, and an explicit rule that correlated legs share one cluster budget. Full Kelly is not used anywhere because our probabilities are estimates with error and Kelly's optimum assumes they are true.
rows.params: Kelly fraction (default 0.25), max unit per single (default 1.0), cluster cap (default 2.0) — defaults, not validated

sections.title: B. Signal inventory (candidates, each with a falsifiable test)
sections.description: A signal is a hypothesis with a stated direction, the market it applies to, the gate that kills it, and the reason it might be real. Nothing here is claimed to work. Publishing them before testing is the point: it makes the graveyard auditable and the multiple-comparison count honest.

rows.name: Home underdog after a failed cover
rows.thesis: Published evidence that sportsbooks under-value home teams, most visibly substantial home underdogs that did not cover the previous week.
rows.test: Must beat the close by a positive mean CLV over >= 300 bets with a 95% lower bound above zero, out of sample.

rows.name: Totals quadratic in the closing line
rows.thesis: Published evidence that Overs cover more often at very small and very large closing totals, implying a nonlinear market bias rather than a uniform one.
rows.test: Fit the curvature out of sample; if the quadratic term's interval includes zero, retire the signal and record the retirement.

rows.name: Prev-season-record overreaction
rows.thesis: Published evidence that bettors over-react to a team's prior-season record and under-regress it; in a totals-style market this shows up as a systematic mispricing of the rebuilt team.
rows.test: Effect must survive a season-by-season split and must not be driven by a handful of teams.

rows.name: Injury-report delta, not level
rows.thesis: The market reprices on the change; the tradeable event is a starter moving from Limited-plus-Questionable to Out, or the reverse. Whether the market over- or under-reacts to that delta is exactly what has to be measured (GAP-17).
rows.test: Regression of line move on availability delta; require the residual to have a stable sign out of sample.

rows.name: Defensive back-half deficiency
rows.thesis: Two outside starters and a deep-middle safety out in the same week (as in our verified Week 10 sample) is a coverage-shell problem that no additive injury count captures; the interaction, not the count, is the signal.
rows.test: Interaction term must beat the additive model on out-of-sample log-loss before it is allowed in the deficiency index.

rows.name: Offensive line cohesion loss
rows.thesis: Interior-line absences show up in run blocking and sack rate before they show up in the box score's headline, so a two-absence interior week is a pattern worth its own term.
rows.market: Sack props, rushing attempts, team total
rows.test: Effect must persist after controlling for the opponent's pass rush quality.

rows.name: Short-week (Thursday) spot
rows.thesis: A four-day preparation compresses install and favours the simpler game plan; the roster rules also make the gameday active count and elevations matter more, so the replacement effect is larger.
rows.market: Total (lower), spread against the more complex offence
rows.test: Must not be a rest-vs-rest artefact; require it in both halves of the sample.

rows.name: QB regime change
rows.thesis: A backup quarterback shifts both the mean and the shape of a team's scoring distribution, and public reaction tends to over-adjust the spread while under-adjusting the total.
rows.test: Compare to a matched sample of same-club games with QB1; require a CLV-positive residual.

rows.name: Designation-by-omission
rows.thesis: Because a player certain to play is left off the game-status list, 'unlisted despite a DNP earlier in the week' is a positive availability signal that a naive pipeline drops as missing data.
rows.test: Precision/recall of the inference against final inactive lists; if we cannot predict activation better than 'listed Questionable', discard.

rows.name: Rest-row filtering
rows.thesis: Club-side reports list non-injury rest cases among the same rows as injuries; a pipeline that counts DNPs without filtering rest will systematically overstate injury burden late in the season.
rows.test: Compare DNP counts with and without rest rows against actual starters; require the correction to improve availability prediction.

rows.name: Reverse favourite-longshot bias on the money line
rows.thesis: Published evidence of bettors overbetting favourites on the money line, with season-varying and unpredictable magnitude — which is precisely why it must be measured continuously rather than adopted as a rule.
rows.test: Stratify by implied probability decile; the effect must persist in the current regime, not only in the 2007-2016 window studied.

rows.name: Correlation arbitrage inside SGPs
rows.thesis: If an operator's combined price under-prices a dependence our joint model captures (or over-prices it), there is a real edge; the house rules already tell us which dependencies they refuse to price outside an SGP.
rows.test: Requires measured operator correlation (GAP-01); the gate is our implied versus theirs, with a variance check because SGP hold is wider.
rows.expect: UNVERIFIED — hold magnitude unknown to us

rows.name: Selective abstention as the meta-signal
rows.thesis: Given the sample-size arithmetic, the highest-value rule in the system is the one that says no: raising the edge threshold converts unmeasurable small edges into fewer, larger ones.
rows.test: Compare realised CLV and detectability at each threshold; publish the curve rather than picking a threshold rhetorically.

rows.name: Referee-crew and officiating tendencies
rows.thesis: Plausible but disallowed: the subject matter is a league-prohibited market class and there is no official published assignment feed we could cite.

sections.title: C. What we refuse to state
sections.description: The line between a specification and a fabrication, drawn explicitly so a reviewer can check we kept it.

rows.item: Any coefficient, prior mean, or effect size presented as settled. Every parameter above is blank with an estimator attached, because inventing a number to make the model look complete is the failure mode the brief prohibits.
Any percentage mapping from a designation to a probability of playing. The league's definitions are qualitative, and the widely-quoted 'Questionable = 50%' has no official basis we could verify.
Any Nevada or per-market hold percentage. The regulator documents exist and are the right source; we have not opened them at page level, so the figure is a gap (GAP-08), not a number.
Any historical injury row we did not fetch. Only the Week 10 2026 chunk we captured is published, and it is labelled partial.
Any claim that a strategy is profitable, or that a backtest is evidence. Until a strategy passes the gates on out-of-sample data with a measured hold, the correct statement about it is 'untested'.
Any use of non-public information about availability, and any bet whose subject is an injury, an official, a single play, or a pre-determined roster decision — the league's own prohibited classes.
